Redundancy is per side - front/rear 1 and 4 - with an LC Switch behind both."},"docsis-non-redundant":{"bays":{"front-0":"casa/us-16x8@1","front-1":"casa/us-16x8@1","front-2":"casa/smm-8x10g@1","front-3":"casa/smm-8x10g@1","front-4":"casa/ds-8x96@1","front-5":"casa/ds-8x96@1","pem-1":"casa/c40g-pem@1","pem-2":"casa/c40g-pem@1","rear-0":"casa/rfu-16x8@1","rear-1":"casa/rfu-16x8@1","rear-2":"casa/blank-faceplate@1","rear-3":"casa/blank-faceplate@1","rear-4":"casa/rfd@1","rear-5":"casa/rfd@1"},"description":"Non-redundant chassis. The guide: \"The Casa C40G chassis is available in both redundant and non-redundant versions.\" There are no switch modules at all - rear 2 and 3 carry blank filler plates where the redundant schemes carry the SMM Switch pair, and rear 1 and 4 carry I/O rather than an LC Switch. Front DS cards pair with QAM IO behind them and front US cards with US IO, which is the classic split architecture rather than the BDM one."}},"description":"Casa C40G CMTS/CCAP - 6RU, 6 paired front/rear slots. Takes the same line cards as the C100G but HORIZONTALLY, so the card is one model placed at rotate 90.","format":1,"gaps":[{"note":"The PEM band's BOTTOM edge at 264.5 is agreed by every source and is not in doubt. Its TOP edge is known only to about 2 mm, and the three candidates each have support: 194.0 is the direct reading of Figure 1-4 and is impossible, because the card slot above ends at 194.82; 194.82 is flush against that slot; 196.0 is what the bays carry and is what the manifest now uses, on the argument that 194.82 is an accumulation of six DERIVED slot pitches (426.6 mm over 14 slots on the C100G, carried across) and that the front face shows a measured 1.48 mm margin in the equivalent position. That argument is sound but it is an argument, not a measurement, and the whole disagreement is six pixels at 2.982 px/mm. A tape measure on a real C40G, or any Casa drawing that dimensions the rear panel, would settle it in one number. FIGURE 1-12 HAS NOW BEEN LOOKED AT AND DOES NOT SETTLE IT, recorded so nobody spends the search twice. \"C40G power entry module\" is the only isolated drawing of this part and the first independent look anything has had at it. Its body measures 866 x 381 px for an aspect of 2.273. The modelled 158.0 x 68.5 is 2.307 and the superseded 158.0 x 70.5 is 2.241, and 2.273 lands 0.04 percent off the midpoint of those two - at 158.0 wide it implies a height of 69.51. IT IS EQUIDISTANT AND CONFIRMS NEITHER. This guide's isolated part drawings are in any case demonstrably about 10 percent wrong about their own aspect - Figure 1-20 draws a card at 12.54 whose real aspect is 11.34 - so a 1.5 percent lean is well inside the drawing's own error. THE NUMBER IS THEREFORE NOT MOVED. It has been moved twice already, in both directions, and a third move on evidence that splits the difference would be the reconciliation loop rather than an escape from it. What Figure 1-12 does confirm is the ARRANGEMENT, which is what a figure is good for: a bolted terminal cover across the top with three fasteners, a minus pair of studs above a plus pair inside two outlined blocks, two release levers standing proud of the body top and bottom, and the yellow disconnect-power label to their right - all of which casa/c40g-pem draws. RECORDED BECAUSE THE MODULE AND THE BAY NOW AGREE, which means nothing will ever flag this again - the fit check that found the original 2 mm discrepancy is satisfied by both being wrong together as easily as by both being right.","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["pem-1","pem-2"],"wanted":"a dimensioned C40G rear elevation, or a tape measure on the PEM opening","what":"pem-band-top-edge"},{"note":"The BDM2/BDM2m datasheet states \"Total Power 300 W\" in a technical specifications table headed \"BDM2/2 m with 6+12 IO Card\", whose RF connector row describes that card's six downstream and twelve upstream ports. The figure is the assembly's. A BDM position is TWO modules here - casa/bdm in a front bay and casa/io-6p12 in the paired rear bay, which is why casa/bdm already carries `pairs-with` - and no document we hold divides the 300 W between them. Writing it onto the front module would make the chassis total come out right and the answer to \"what does a BDM front module draw\" come out wrong, so neither half carries a figure and the chassis total stays a floor. The arithmetic does not settle it either way: 12 x 300 W lands on the C100G's stated 3.6 kW whether the 300 W is the pair or the front half with small rear cards. THE THREE REAR RF I/O CARDS ADDED LATER FALL ON THE SAME SIDE OF THIS AS THE 6+12. casa/rfd, casa/rfu-16x8 and casa/ups-32x4 carry NO power figure, because Tables A-8 and A-9 give their port counts and connector types and no watts at all, and every figure Casa does publish for the slot is already the pair's - Table A-3 heads the DQM column \"Maximum consumption with I/O module\" and Table A-4 gives \"Single DCU w/ RFU I/O\" 200 W against \"Single DCU w/ RFU UPS 32x4 I/O\" 220 W for the same US16x8. Subtracting one from the other to get a rear card's share would be our arithmetic and would also be the wrong subtraction - the 20 W is the difference between two PAIRINGS, not between two I/O cards.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["casa/bdm2@1","casa/bdm2m@1","casa/bdm@1","casa/ds-8x192@1","casa/ds-8x8@1","casa/ds-8x96@1","casa/io-6p12-io2@1","casa/io-6p12-sw-io2@1","casa/io-6p12-sw@2","casa/io-6p12@2","casa/rfd@1","casa/rfu-16x8@1","casa/ups-32x4@1","casa/us-16x4@1","casa/us-16x8@1"],"wanted":"a pairable unit that can carry properties, so that a figure measured on a pair can be attached to the pair. The scope is now DATA - every card here declares `power-draw-scope: module-with-paired-io`, so a chassis sum knows not to add the rear partner and L30 catches it if one gains its own figure - but the scope says only THAT the figure covers a pair, not WHICH pair. The C100G HIG gives the same US16x8 200 W with the RFU I/O and 220 W with the RFU UPS 32x4, and the manifest can carry only one of them. Asking for \"a per-module figure\" was the wrong question: Casa states none, and one may not exist to be divided out. What is missing is the mechanism, and enough vendors doing this to design one from - Casa is the only one in the corpus.","what":"paired-module-power"},{"blocks":[],"note":"Casa rates a power ENTRY module in amps and volts, never in watts. Table A-1 gives \"DC current 20A nominal per feed @ -48VDC\" and the PEM section says the modules \"receive -40.5 to -60 VDC (-48VDC nominal) power from separate 20A power supply sources\" - but no document states a wattage, and deriving one means choosing a point the vendor left open: two current figures across a voltage range put V x I anywhere from about 810 W to 1800 W per feed. A power entry module also does not convert or regulate; it filters and distributes what the plant feeds it, so its rating is a current-carrying limit rather than the continuous output power-output-w means. The stated volts and amps are recorded in the contract's attrs; the L27 warning stays standing as the record that the watt figure is missing.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["casa/c40g-pem@1"],"wanted":"a wattage for the C40G power entry module from Casa - a nameplate photograph of the module itself would do it, or any document that rates it in watts rather than amps","what":"power-entry-rating"}],"groups":{"cooling":{"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"Fan module"},"front-slots":{"index-origin":1,"role":"traffic","term":"Slot"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"power":{"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"PEM"},"rear-slots":{"index-origin":1,"role":"traffic","term":"Slot"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"Casa Systems","maturity":"modelled","model":"C40G","name":"c40g","portfolio":{"family":"CMTS/CCAP"},"provenance":{"ac-variant":"drawing - the C40G ships AC or DC and the guide draws the rear both ways: Figures 1-2 and 1-3 for the AC chassis, 1-4 and 1-5 for the DC one. The AC build puts \"up to four removable 1100W AC power supply units\" in a row across the bottom FRONT, behind the snap-on cover, in place of the two DC power entry modules at the bottom rear. Figure 1-10 shows them with the cover off and Figure 1-11 shows their other end. Numbering runs right to left - \"PSUs are labeled on the front of the chassis as PSU1, PSU2, PSU3 and PSU4 from right to left\" - so the LEFTMOST bay is psu-4, and rel-pos follows the vendor rather than the drawing order. THIS IS AN ORTHOGONAL AXIS to the other two configurations, which are redundancy schemes: an AC chassis can run either scheme. Configurations are the only mechanism the format has for a variant, so the axes share one list; ac-power changes nothing about redundancy and neither BDM scheme says anything about power. The PEM bays therefore default EMPTY and each DC scheme names them, because a configuration cannot clear a bay - occupants are strings - and because neither AC nor DC is \"the\" C40G. THE AC REAR FACE IS BUILT BUT NOT PLACED. Figures 1-2 and 1-3 show it: one bolted panel across the bottom of the rear carrying a rocker switch and an IEC C14 inlet per PSU, where the DC chassis carries its two PEMs. It is modelled as casa/c40g-ac-inlet-panel@1 and left unplaced, because the format cannot say that a bolted panel is present only in one configuration: a configuration carries bays, skins, airflow, region-context and part-numbers, but not placements. Making it a bay instead would overlap the two PEM bays in the same band, which L13 rejects - and a bay cannot use `for:` to declare that overlap legitimate, because L13 builds its owned-set from placements only. `optional:` would hide it everywhere, since build.sh emits no --with variants. So the AC rear renders as an empty band today and the part is measured and waiting.","chassis":"datasheet - Table A-1 of the C40G Hardware Installation Guide (rev 07/07/2022): 10.47in (265.90mm) H, 19in (482mm) W, 15.25in (388.45mm) D, 6RU","fan-modules":"drawing - Figure 1-7, \"C40G fan module location and directional air flow\", settles which side is which and it is NOT symmetric. The RIGHT strip is labelled \"System fan module\" and \"Air filter\" with \"Air flow direction IN\"; the LEFT strip is labelled \"Secondary fan module slot (optional with redundancy kit)\" with \"Air flow direction OUT\". So fan-right defaults to a module and fan-left defaults to empty, which is what a chassis without the redundancy kit actually looks like. Both strips carry the same FAN TRAY 2 / FAN TRAY 1 / AIR FILTER legend printed on the CHASSIS, which is why an empty left slot still shows it in the guide figures","front-furniture":"drawing-measured - Figure 1-1, \"Casa C40G CMTS front view\", PASSES the orthographic gate. Its chassis renders 1364 x 760 px for an aspect of 1.795 against a true rack face of 482 / 265.9 = 1.813, agreeing to 1 percent, so unlike the isolated card figures it carries geometry - at 2.858 px/mm scaled by the exactly known 265.9 height. Measured off it in body coordinates: the two vertical fan strips at x 1.5-37.5 and 386.7-422.7, both running y 17-222; the card band x 37.5-386.4, which independently confirms the existing card bays at x 42.0 width 345.5; the brand band y 196.3-222.9; and the snap-on PSU cover y 226.7-264.9. The right fan bay is trimmed to start at x 388.0 so it does not overlap the card bays, which end at 387.5","non-redundant-variant":"drawing plus prose - ADDED, because the guide draws four rear views and the model only had three configurations for them. Figures 1-2 and 1-4 are the AC and DC NON-REDUNDANT rears and 1-3 and 1-5 the redundant pair, so the four figures are two axes crossed - AC/DC and redundant/not - not four layouts. The AC/DC axis was already modelled as ac-power; this entry adds the other value of the second axis. The layout is stated in words as well as drawn: \"Rear slots (non-redundant system) - Upstream and downstream line card I/O slots: 0, 1, 4 5; Blank filler plates: 2, 3\", against the redundant list right below it which reads \"I/O slots: 0, 5; LC Switch slots: 1, 4; SMM Switch slots: 2, 3\". Figure 1-4 is legible at 4x and agrees: slots 5 and 4 read QAM IO, 3 and 2 are plain plates with one screw at each end, and 1 and 0 read US IO. The chassis overview also says outright that \"The Casa C40G chassis is available in both redundant and non-redundant versions\". THE FRONT IS NOT MODELLED FROM A NON-REDUNDANT FIGURE - there is no separate front view for it - so front 0/1/4/5 take the DS and US cards Figure 1-1 draws (DS 8X96 above, US 16X8 below) on the pairing the rear figure shows, QAM IO behind a DS card and US IO behind a US one, and front 2/3 keep the SMM pair, which the front-slot bullet lists without qualifying it by redundancy. That pairing is an inference from two figures and is the softest part of this entry","orientation":"Jason, confirmed against Fig 1-1 - the C40G takes the SAME line cards as the C100G but on their side, so every bay is rotate 90","power-entry":"drawing-measured - Figure 1-4, \"C40G CMTS rear view (DC; non-redundant)\", scaled by the known 265.9 height at 2.982 px/mm. The two PEM faces read x 44.8-195.7 and 212.8-377.7 and the band runs y 194-264.5. They are bays and not placements because the guide carries both \"Removing the DC power entry modules\" and \"Replacing the PEMs\" and they slide into openings. THE BAYS WERE RIGHT AND THE COMPONENT WAS WRONG, and I got that backwards once before landing here. casa/c40g-pem read 158.0 x 70.5 against bays of 158.0 x 68.5 - a module 2.00 mm TALLER than the opening it slides into, found by asr9k-cards' bay-versus-occupant sweep. Nothing else could see it: L13 fires on overlap, so a bay too SMALL for what it accepts is invisible, and 2 mm is invisible drawn. THREE CANDIDATES FOR THE BAND'S TOP EDGE, and the arithmetic decides between them. 194.0 is what this entry and the component's both read off Figure 1-4, and it is IMPOSSIBLE - the card slot above, rear-0, ends at 164.35 + 30.47 = 194.82, and two pieces of sheet metal cannot share 0.82 mm. 194.82 itself is flush against that edge. 196.0 is what the bays already said. 196.0 WINS BECAUSE 194.82 IS THE SOFTEST NUMBER OF THE THREE AND FLUSH-MOUNTING ON IT WOULD MAKE THIS BAND DEPEND ON IT EXACTLY. That 30.47 slot pitch is not a measurement of a slot: it is 426.6 mm of card region from the C100G's Figure 1-1 divided by 14, carried across to this chassis, and rear-0's bottom edge is that derived pitch ACCUMULATED SIX TIMES from y 12.0. The error compounds. Against that, 196.0 leaves a 1.18 mm margin below the card cage - and the front face, measured independently, shows a 1.48 mm margin in exactly that position between the card band and the brand band at y 196.3. A structural margin confirmed on one face is better evidence than a flush fit against an accumulation of derived pitches. SO THE FIGURE READING OF 194 IS THE OVERREAD, by about two millimetres at 2.982 px/mm, which is six pixels. casa/c40g-pem is corrected to 68.5 to match the opening it goes into. THE HONEST RANGE IS 2 mm and a tape measure could still move this - see the pem-band-top-edge gap. The team lead flagged rear-0 as the softest of the three before I had finished, and they were right: my first attempt grew the bays onto that edge, which traded a fit defect for a dependency on the least trustworthy number in the file. NOTE THE VARIANT SPLIT: this is the DC chassis, and the AC one is modelled too - see the ac-variant entry. An AC C40G carries four 1100 W PSUs behind the snap-on front cover instead of these two PEMs, which is why these bays default EMPTY and each DC configuration names them.","protecting-slots":"SETTLED, and the same half-fault as the C100G. The guide numbers this one twice over. For the classic scheme the chassis overview reads \"Rear slots (fully redundant system) - Upstream and downstream line card I/O slots: 0, 5; LC Switch slots: 1, 4; SMM Switch slots: 2, 3\", Table A-2 agrees with \"Two LC Switch modules for DOCSIS-module redundancy in rear slots 1 and 4\", and Figure 1-5, the rear view OF THAT EXACT LAYOUT, is legible at 4x: slots 5 to 0 read QAM IO, LC SWITCH, SMM SWITCH, SMM SWITCH, LC SWITCH, US IO. So rear-4 is an LC Switch in the classic scheme, and docsis-classic said so in its description while placing a switched I/O. For the BDM scheme the guide is equally explicit - \"C40G rear side (3+1): Slot 1 - LC-BDM-SWITCH; Slot 4 - 6+12 SW-IO or 6+12 SW-IO2\" - so bdm-3plus1 was right and is unchanged. rear-4 accepts both, and each configuration names its own","rear-order":"NOT mirrored, unlike the C100G. Walking round a chassis flips left to right, not top to bottom - and these cards stack vertically, so rear 5 stays at the top where front 5 is","rear-slots":"photograph - a C40G rear shows plain 6+12 I/O in slots 0 and 5, the 6+12 SW I/O in slot 4, and SMM-SW-BDM B and A in 3 and 2. Slot 1 takes the LC-BDM-SWITCH that protects, per the 3+1 scheme","redundancy-prose":"REMOVED, not lost. attrs.other carried `redundancy: \"3+1 with BDM (slot 1 protects, slot 4 active); classic DOCSIS protects per side at 1 and 4\"` - one prose sentence restating what the two redundancy configurations now say structurally, bay by bay. It was worth keeping only while the bays were wrong about it, which they were until the protecting-slots fix: the sentence was the correct statement and the model contradicted it. Now the model IS the statement, and a second copy that no tool can read is the thing rule 8 warns about. The AC axis is a third configuration and was never in this sentence at all","side-faces":"drawing plus a stated absence, exactly as on the C100G. NO FIGURE IN THIS GUIDE SHOWS THE TOP, BOTTOM OR SIDE FACES either - Figures 1-1 through 1-5 are front and rear elevations and 1-7 is an airflow diagram. So the four are sized from Table A-1 (\"Height: 10.47 in. (265.90 mm), Depth: 15.25 in. (388.45 mm)\"; its 19 in / 482 mm width is the rack face including the flanges, so the 432.95 body width is used) and carry only the integral mounting flanges and the chassis label, which the guide locates in the same words the C100G guide uses - \"The C40G product label is affixed to the top front side of the chassis\". Orientation matches the C100G: top and bottom put the front at y = 0, left puts it at x = 0, right mirrors it. NO SIDE VENTS ARE DRAWN, deliberately, and this is the judgement call worth flagging. Air goes right to left through this chassis, so the side panels are a plausible place for an intake and an exhaust - but the filter the guide describes is on the FAN MODULEs own face (\"Figure 1-9 shows the air filter side of the fan module\"), the fan modules are inserted from the front, and no figure shows an opening in either side panel. Drawing vents on a guess is the wrong-box outcome these views exist to prevent","slot-compatibility":"drawing - the C40G guide numbers its own slots twice. The chassis overview lists \"Front slots - Upstream and downstream line card slots: 0, 1, 4 5; Active and standby SMM slots: 2 and 3\", and Table A-2, \"C40G capacities\", agrees: \"6 line card slots on front - 1 Switch and Management (SMM) module, 1 SMM redundant module, 4 DOCSIS modules (any combination of DS and US modules)\". So front-2 and front-3 take the SMM generations and the other four take every DS and US card, \"any combination\" being a real statement modelled as it reads. Table A-2's DQM row names DS8x8, DS8x96 and DS8x192 and its DCU row names US16x4 and US16x8, so all five are eligible here even though THIS guide's Tables A-3 and A-4 print power for only three of them - the C100G guide carries the other two. The CSC is placed by its data sheet, \"The C40G can house 4 CSCs for a maximum of 32 ports\", which is the same four slots. The rear is deliberately NOT widened: the same overview puts LC Switch in rear 1 and 4, SMM Switch in rear 2 and 3, and I/O cards in the rest, and it is the only place either guide says where blank filler plates go by number - \"Rear slots (non-redundant system) - Blank filler plates: 2, 3\". Bay defaults are unchanged","slot-order":"drawing + photograph - slots run 5 at the TOP down to 0 at the bottom, printed on the chassis, with 3 and 2 in red as the SMM pair","switch-slot-print":"drawing - a free check that PASSES. Figure 1-20 of this guide, \"BDM module, SMM Switch BDM A, B, and LC Switch BDM\", prints each SMM Switch card's slot assignment on its own faceplate, for BOTH chassis: A reads \"C100G Slot 6 / C40G Slot 2\" and B reads \"C100G Slot 7 / C40G Slot 3\". rear-2 accepts casa/smm-sw-bdm-a@1 and rear-3 accepts casa/smm-sw-bdm-b@1, which is what the card says. The same figure is Figure 1-14 of the C100G guide and that device's switch-slot-print entry records the other half","width":"body 432.95, the same as the C100G - both are 19in rack devices and the ears sit outside that.
